opus.why: One screenshot, one yes/no question: is the button cropped. This is an obvious visual check that needs no deep judgment.

fable.why: Single screenshot, one yes/no visual check on a possibly subtle clip; Sonnet's vision is reliable enough here and no reasoning depth is needed. Haiku risks missing a 2–3px crop.

opus.why: Fine-grained comparison of character consistency and hand anatomy across stills. Opus's stronger vision matters for catching subtle drift. Output is short and well scoped.

fable.why: Fine-grained continuity (jacket, hair) across three stills plus hand anatomy in a cropped region; this is exactly where weaker vision misses defects, and studio continuity errors are costly.

opus.why: Agentic setup (dev server, two viewports) plus a precise pixel, hex and weight diff against a mockup, ranked by how visible each gap is. Precise visual comparison benefits from Opus. The task is well specified, so medium is enough.

fable.why: Agentic (dev server, two-viewport screenshots) plus a precise pixel-level visual diff against a mockup; needs to cross-check CSS/DOM to report real px, weights and hex values and rank by visibility.

opus.why: A well-specified Playwright walk through the checkout with screenshots at each step. Spotting layout breaks and overlaps is standard work that Sonnet at high handles reliably.

fable.why: Long multistep Playwright run on two viewports with visual overlap detection on every step, a tricky keyboard-open simulation, and a hard 'don't place an order' constraint; Sonnet could drive the browser but is more likely to miss layout defects or botch the keyboard check.

opus.why: The owner is frustrated after a missed regression. The job needs an exhaustive page-by-page check of the PDF against the HTML, a fix that reaches every glow, and before/after proof. Brand visual quality and thoroughness are critical.

fable.why: Brand asset, user already burned by partial fixes; must exhaustively compare every PDF page against HTML, find all remaining glow instances across the PDF pipeline, fix, and produce before/after screenshots. Thoroughness over a long agentic run is the whole task.

opus.why: Applying an .otp master through LibreOffice needs tricky automation (UNO or headless), and each slide must then be scored visually against brand criteria. A long agentic task where judgment counts.

fable.why: Applying a master via LibreOffice (likely UNO/CLI scripting), exporting PNGs, then scoring brand criteria (hex colors, 48px margins, logo overlap) requires combining visual review with inspecting the pptx itself; brand judgment under an ask-before-install constraint.

opus.why: Inspecting one still against a checklist: finger counts, a duplicated cup, fake chalkboard text. Detail-level vision is where Opus beats Sonnet. Scope is tight.

fable.why: Tightly specified single-still review, but the checks are finger count, cup duplication and fake chalkboard text, which demand top vision fidelity; little reasoning needed beyond the checklist, so medium effort.

opus.why: Checking four notes against stills and clips, including pulling frames at 1.2–1.8s, then making a regeneration call. Needs reliable detection of visual artifacts and sound judgment.

fable.why: Must open stills and extract clip frames (ffmpeg at 1.2–1.8s), verify each note including overruling the user's judge, and decide what truly needs regeneration; agentic plus multiple fine visual judgments.

opus.why: Judging palette, lighting direction and grain against an approved moodboard, then rewriting a client-facing image prompt. Brand and visual judgment drive the outcome, and the deliverable is short.

fable.why: Client-approved moodboard match on palette, lighting direction and grain is brand/visual judgment where drops show, and the rewritten image prompt is a creative deliverable that must hit those attributes precisely.
